body:
🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 9)
Channel: alert-system (+ alert-runtime-monitoring)  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 3
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `DevOps` (`@devops` / `#team-devops`) for the SQL cluster; affected: `Vertical App Experience` (runtime-core-api), `CRM Experience` (Portals). Inert text.

Symptoms:
  - Sun 06:31–06:38Z (01:31 ET): runtime-core-api p90 breached on all 4 runtime hosts (prod-rt-01..04). 10-min avg p90 was 2.78s against a 2.0s threshold, and the 10s-resolution p90 peaked at 72.8s. RTC Screen Load / RTC Action p95, PortalApps 5xx Warn (1 error on 8 requests) and a Watchdog latency story on runtime/load co-fired.
  - The slow part was SQL, not app code. Trivial statements took seconds: `SELECT TOP … FROM PreferencesMethod` 25.2s, `INSERT INTO accInvoice` 17.9s, `spiderColumns` 9.8s. 91 SQL spans >3s between 06:20 and 06:50Z across runtime-core-api, sync-queue-consumer, rest-api, classic/method, approutine-subscriber and portal apps, all on `methoddbclus1` / `sql-prod-1`.
  - Mongo spans stayed ≤0.01s. The 8 "Redis operation cancelled" errors come from requests that were already cancelled, not from Redis itself: 0 Redis timeouts, so ki-2026-07-06 is refuted.
  - *This happens every Sunday.* Slow-SQL spans (>3s) in the same 06:20–06:50Z window: 82 on Sun 11-08, 58 on Sun 11-15, 91 today, vs 0–3 on Fri/Sat. The same monitor cluster fired 11-08 06:31–06:49Z and 11-15 06:34–06:44Z, plus 11-01 at 05:45Z (before the DST change). It follows ~01:30 America/New_York.

Trace IDs: 6b028c6c00000000be878bdbff0e04e2 (21.7s action, INSERT accInvoice 17.9s), 6b028d870000000033b1f024dde78c16 (43.5s screen load → 408, PreferencesMethod SELECT 25.2s)
Likely cause: a scheduled weekly SQL job on cluster 1 (index rebuild, CHECKDB or full backup) at ~01:30 ET Sunday that blocks or starves normal queries for ~7 min. *Not confirmed from the SQL side.* The bot has no SQL tunnel this session, so it couldn't read the SQL Agent schedule.
Suggested next action: DevOps/DBA: check the SQL Agent / maintenance-plan schedule on methoddbclus1 for a Sunday ~01:30 ET job, then move it or make it ONLINE/resumable. User impact is low at that hour but real (some 408/400s). Once it's confirmed I'll add a KB entry so the Sunday co-fires classify automatically.

Source alerts (3 total, degraded cycle so no permalinks):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/17872725 runtime-core-api p90, Triggered 06:32:45Z → OK 06:42:45Z (alert-system)
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551647 PortalApps 5xx, Warn 06:34:27Z / 06:40:27Z (alert-runtime-monitoring)
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/236570583 Watchdog "New issue to review", Triggered 06:42:03Z (alert-system)

Evidence:
  • DD APM slow SQL spans (91): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=env%3Aprod%20%40duration%3A%3E3s%20%40component%3ASqlClient&start=1795328400000&end=1795330200000
  • DD APM slow runtime-core requests: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20env%3Aprod%20%40duration%3A%3E5s&start=1795328700000&end=1795329900000
  • Last Sunday, same window (58 slow SQL spans): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=env%3Aprod%20%40duration%3A%3E3s%20%40component%3ASqlClient&start=1794723600000&end=1794725400000
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Aruntime-core-api&exp_agg=avg&start=1795327200&end=1795331400
  • Kibana (8 Redis-cancelled errors, downstream of the cancellations): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-22T06:20:00.000Z',to:'2026-11-22T06:50:00.000Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service%3A%22runtime-core-api%22%20and%20message%3A%22Redis%20operation%20cancelled%22'))
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-22-91dd76a8c2cbd96d.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #294 (lifetime count). The companion RTC Screen Load fire this morning is #295 and is suppressed.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (inert)
Playbook: check for p95 points over 3s and confirm it's latency-only (0 error logs). An isolated spike is noise; a sustained run of points warrants an APM drill-down by screen id.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts: monitor 117279738 `RTC Action Execution has a high p95 latency`, Triggered 03:44:18Z, 03:50:18Z and 06:35:18Z → Recovered 06:45:18Z. Companion 115456700 RTC Screen Load fired 06:34Z and 08:16–08:28Z. Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalinks.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/_actionid_*}` 03:30–06:50Z: 197 points, 6 over 3.0s (03:43 3.57s, 04:49 3.57s, 05:19 3.91s, 05:53 3.35s, 06:32 21.54s, 06:35 3.62s). `service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod` returned 0 logs for both 03:38–03:56Z and 08:10–08:40Z, so it's latency-only.
  • 03:4x: isolated slow actions (22.3s @03:49:38Z; 16.2s @03:54:50Z, which includes a 9.5s outbound HTTP call). This is the usual KB shape.
  • The 06:3x episode on both RTC monitors isn't this KB's noise. It's the Sunday ~01:30 ET SQL stall on cluster 1, posted separately as needs-human (91dd76a8).

Evidence:
  • DD APM traces >3s, 03:38–03:56Z: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20env%3Aprod%20%40duration%3A%3E3s&start=1795318680000&end=1795319760000
  • DD APM traces >3s, 08:10–08:40Z (screen-load episode): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20env%3Aprod%20%40duration%3A%3E3s&start=1795335000000&end=1795336800000
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Aruntime-core-api&exp_agg=avg&start=1795318200&end=1795337100
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/117279738
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-22-db94a5b0e065c139.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #186 (lifetime count). It posts because the 24h suppression window lapsed: the last post was 11-21 at 14:21Z, about 24h50m before this cycle ran. Measured from the first fire (14:13Z), the gap is 23h52m, which would have suppressed it. This cycle followed the cycle-time convention.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`customer-management` usergroup / `#team-customer-management`, inert)
Playbook: confirm the dip is a brief drop below the fixed 2 msg/s floor (not a data gap), confirm 0 `status:error` logs, and treat it as quiet-period noise. Escalate only if a fire stays open >1h or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (3 total): monitor 302057011 `[CRM] runtime-core-subscriber throughput dropped (possible stall)`. It triggered at 14:13:31Z, 14:17:31Z and 14:35:31Z, and had recovered by 14:36:31Z. This was a degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so there are no permalinks.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:runtime-core-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()` 13:30-14:50Z: 160 points, 70 of them below 2 msg/s. The dip ran ~14:00-14:33Z with a minimum of 0.23/s at 14:10Z and never reached 0. Throughput was back to 3-8 msg/s from 14:33Z, against 22-181 msg/s before 14:00Z.
  • `service:runtime-core-subscriber status:error env:prod` 14:00-14:45Z returned 0 logs. No sibling monitor co-fired, and every trigger self-recovered within 1-17 min.
  • This is the same quiet-period-against-a-fixed-floor shape as every prior occurrence (Sunday midday traffic). There is no error or stall signal.
  • 186 fires since 07-02 with no confirmed real stall. A relative or anomaly threshold (or a longer window) on this monitor family would remove most of this noise.

Evidence:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795354200&end=1795359000
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302057011
